newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up as investors focus on economy.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up as investors focus on economy.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Thursday as investors focused on the economy's solid growth prospects for this year and rumors about political instability lost force, brokers said.

But recent media reports about both a possible armed conflict between Peru and nieighboring Ecuador and political maneuvers to create a military coup steered players to focus their buys on firms with solid long-term prospects, they added. The General Index IGRA rose 1.94 percent to 2,167.4 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index ISEL dropped 1.68 percent to 3,115.6 points.
In a total of 2,120 trades, volume was 33.0 million soles ($12.5 million).

The mining sector saw most gains due mainly to high zinc prices. Benchmark Telefonica del Peru received a boost because Societe Generale started its coverage of the telecom as buy and Peru's largest brewery group Union de Cervecerias Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA climbed on the announcement of a share dividend.
Investors were likely to concentrate their funds on these stocks Friday and lift the market up slightly overall, brokers said.

The metal price and company news Thursday "made investors forget -- at least for the time being -- the problems that the country faces. But the recommendations were to buy stocks that are solid for the long-term to protect investors against any eventuality", said Pablo Navarro of local brokerage Fortuna.
Telefonica ended Thursday up 1.62 percent at 6.90 soles on volume of 937,000 shares.
Backus climbed 0.75 percent to 2.70 soles on volume of 1.5 million shares. Polymetallic miner Morococha climbed 4.10 percent to close at 6.10 soles on 83,000 shares.
